name: ADS131M08IPBSR
title: ADS131M08: 8-channel simultaneous-sampling 24-bit delta-sigma ADC, 32 kSPS, PGA to 128, TQFP-32 / WQFN-32
summary: An eight-channel analog front-end for energy metering, power metrology and circuit breakers: eight delta-sigma ADCs sample together at up to 32 kSPS, each with a PGA from 1 to 128, a decimation filter, per-channel phase delay in 244 ns steps (at 8.192 MHz) and offset and gain correction registers. A 1.2 V reference, a negative charge pump for inputs below ground, CRC on SPI traffic and on the register map, fast startup and a low-power current-detect mode are built in. AVDD and DVDD run from 2.7 V to 3.6 V (DVDD down to 1.65 V with the core LDO bypassed). The package is a 5 mm TQFP-32 or a 4 mm WQFN-32, rated -40 °C to +125 °C.

circuits.title: Recommended antialiasing filter
circuits.description: A first-order differential RC low-pass for each channel input: a 1 kΩ resistor in each leg and 10 nF across the two outputs, which go to one channel's AINxP and AINxN. The values hold for CLKIN between 2 MHz and 8.2 MHz.

circuits.title: Minimum interface connections
circuits.description: The fewest host lines: a local LVCMOS oscillator clocks CLKIN, SYNC/RESET is tied to DVDD, CS is tied to DGND, and the host keeps step through DRDY on one of its GPIOs. SCLK, DIN and DOUT go to the host's SCLK, MOSI and MISO.
notes: Alternatives: CLKIN from the host's CLKOUT instead of the oscillator; SYNC/RESET to a host GPIO instead of DVDD (one of SYNC/RESET or DRDY goes to the host); CS from the host's CS instead of DGND.
With CS held low, the input and output CRCs are to be enabled and checked.

circuits.title: Three-phase current and voltage front-end with neutral current
circuits.description: Metering a three-phase star load. Current transformers on phases A, B and C and on the neutral each drive one channel (0, 2, 4, 6) across a burden resistor; a resistive divider from each phase to neutral feeds channels 1, 3 and 5; channel 7 takes an auxiliary signal such as a temperature sensor. Every negative input, the neutral and AGND are one node. Each channel also takes an RC antialiasing filter.
notes: T1 to T4 are the transformer secondaries, pin 1 to the negative input; each primary is the line conductor the transformer encircles. A Rogowski coil can take a transformer's place, with the integration done digitally.
The three-phase metrology design of the typical application uses this same front-end.
The channel 5 divider connects to phase C (printed on phase B).

circuits.title: Voltage measurement front-end
circuits.description: Scales 100 V to 240 V mains for a gain-1 channel. A varistor across live and neutral takes surges; three 300 kΩ resistors in series over 750 Ω divide the line down, giving ±256 mV (182 mVRMS) at 240 V; an RC filter in each leg ahead of the inputs removes out-of-band signals. Neutral is the circuit ground and the channel's negative side.
notes: RFILT and CFILT carry no values in this design.

circuits.title: Current measurement front-end
circuits.description: A current transformer with a 2000:1 turns ratio on the live conductor works into two equal burden resistors in series whose midpoint is ground, so the two ADC inputs swing in antiphase; 2RB totals 12.98 Ω, which gives ±918 mV (649 mVRMS) at 100 A. An RC filter in each leg sets the antialiasing.

parts.note: secondary winding; the primary is the live conductor

notes: RFILT and CFILT carry no values in this design.

circuits.title: Multiple devices on one SPI bus
circuits.description: Several converters sampling together. One host clock drives every CLKIN and one host GPIO strobes every SYNC/RESET, so all devices convert in step; SCLK, DIN and DOUT are shared, each device has its own CS, and only device 1's DRDY goes to the host interrupt.
notes: Device n stands for any further devices, each wired like device 2 with its own CS line.
SYNC/RESET has to be strobed on all devices together at least once to line up their sample periods.

operation.text: Eight delta-sigma converters sample at the same instant, each with its own PGA (gain 1 to 128), decimation filter, phase adjustment and offset and gain correction. The analog side runs from 2.7 V to 3.6 V; the digital side takes 1.8 V or 3.3 V. A built-in negative charge pump lets the inputs go 1.3 V under AGND on a single supply. Above gain 4 an input precharge buffer keeps the input impedance high. In HR mode each channel delivers up to 32 kSPS. Control and data pass over an SPI-compatible port; extra devices share the bus with their own CS lines.

Each analog input has a diode to AVDD for overvoltage. Because the charge pump lets inputs sit below AGND there is no diode to AGND; the same diode clamps negative excursions at its reverse breakdown. External parts must keep inputs inside the absolute maximum voltage and current.
Each channel's MUXn[1:0] bits in CHn_CFG pick the channel's own pins, AGND (inputs shorted, for offset calibration), or the positive or negative DC test signal.

PGAGAINn bits in GAIN1 and GAIN2 set each channel's gain to 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128, and the full-scale range is ±1.2 V divided by the gain. At gains up to 4 the input impedance is 330 kΩ × 4.096 MHz / fMOD (330 kΩ at fMOD = 4.096 MHz); from gain 8 the precharge buffer makes it very high and the input bias current is the useful figure. A low source impedance gives the best gain error, INL and distortion.

The internal band-gap reference is 1.2 V nominal and settles fast enough for fast startup; conversions wait until it has settled. An external reference goes into REFIN with 1.25 V nominal; the full-scale range is then scaled by 1.2/1.25, so 1.3 V on REFIN gives 1.248 V / gain. REFIN must carry no capacitance when current-detect mode is used.

The master clock is either an external clock on CLKIN or the on-chip oscillator with a crystal between XTAL1/CLKIN and XTAL2. Best results need the modulator clock, and so the master clock, synchronous with SCLK: drive CLKIN and read data in step with it, and switch the oscillator off when unused. PWR[1:0] in CLOCK selects high-resolution, low-power or very-low-power mode by scaling bias currents; each mode has its own CLKIN range.

The modulator runs at fMOD = fCLKIN / 2 and pushes its quantization noise to high frequencies. The decimation filter is a linear-phase FIR sinc filter; OSR[2:0] in CLOCK sets the OSR (128 to 16384) and so the data rate and the noise bandwidth. Each channel has two filter paths: a fast-settling sinc1-like path used for the first two conversions after power-up or reset, then the sinc3 path. For OSR 128 to 1024 the sinc3 output is used directly; for 2048 and above sinc3 runs at OSR 1024 followed by a sinc1 averager doing the remaining factor of 2 to 16. The response has nulls at every multiple of the data rate except multiples of fMOD, where it repeats; tones near multiples of fMOD alias.

Enabling a channel, changing its mux or gain, or resynchronizing restarts the filter. Unsettled data are not held back, so the host discards results until the filter settling time for the OSR in use has passed; the next DRDY falling edge after that carries settled data.

An optional first-order high-pass removes offset and low-frequency noise. A nonzero DCBLOCK[3:0] in THRSHLD_LSB turns it on and sets coefficient a and so the corner; DCBLKn_DIS in CHn_CFG excludes single channels. The corner scales with CLKIN and data rate.

A DC test level derived by dividing the internal reference is shared by all channels. It is 2/15 of the full-scale input at any gain: 160 mV at gain 1, 80 mV at gain 2. Global-chop mode cannot read it.

PHASEn[9:0] in CHn_CFG shifts a channel's sample period by a signed number of modulator clocks, to match sensors with different phase responses, such as a voltage divider against a current transformer. The range is -OSR/2 to OSR/2 - 1, limited to -512 to 511 above OSR 1024; out-of-range values are clipped (100 at OSR 128 becomes 63). Shifts of more than half a sample are made by offsetting sample indices in software and trimming the fraction with PHASEn. Phase settings change DRDY timing and are switched off in global-chop mode.

Each channel subtracts its OCALn[23:0] value (24-bit two's complement, same format as the data) and then multiplies by GCALn[23:0] / 2^23 (unsigned, 0 to just under 2). Correction is always active; defaults are 000000h and 800000h, which leave data unchanged. Registers are volatile, so coefficients are rewritten after each power-up.

A 16-bit CRC, CCITT or ANSI by CRC_TYPE, seed FFFFh, covers every word of a frame including padding. The input CRC is off by default and enabled by RX_CRC_EN; on a mismatch no command runs except WREG (which writes anyway), CRC_ERR sets, and the next frame answers as for NULL. The output CRC is always sent at the end of a frame.

With REG_CRC_EN set, the device continuously computes a CRC over registers 02h to 30h, one bit per CLKIN period, MSB of 02h first, and stores it in REGMAP_CRC. Any change, a register write included, sets REG_MAP in STATUS; reading STATUS clears it.

A reset comes from power-on, from SYNC/RESET held low longer than tw(RSL), or from the RESET command (0011h). Registers return to defaults and conversions start once a clock is present. DRDY going high marks the SPI as ready; earlier SPI traffic is ignored. Power-on reset takes tPOR from supplies at 90%. After a pin or command reset the host waits tREGACQ (or for DRDY high). RESET is acted on only after the full ten-word frame; a cut-short frame cancels it.

Once tPOR has passed and CLKIN runs, the modulators start after (256 + 44) tMOD. The first two results come from the fast-settling filter, settled but noisy (1500 µVRMS); from the third the sinc3 path takes over. At OSR 1024 and 8.192 MHz the first data arrive 0.323 ms and sinc3 data 0.823 ms after CLKIN starts. Supply CLKIN as early as possible; skip the first two DRDY falling edges if their noise is too high. Pin and command resets behave the same, without tPOR.
Results arrive at fMOD / OSR, each marked by a DRDY falling edge; this mode suits AC measurement and gives the highest data rates.

GC_EN in CFG makes each channel alternate input polarity on successive internal conversions and average pairs, cancelling the PGA and ADC offset and its drift (offset in external circuits is untouched). The filter resets at each swap, so three internal conversions make one result; GC_DLY[3:0] adds 2 to 65536 tMOD after each swap for external circuits to settle. The conversion period is tGC_DLY + 3 × OSR × tMOD, and the first after a restart is two such periods plus 44 tMOD; a SYNC/RESET falling edge or an OSR change restarts all channels together. Noise falls by √2; phase calibration is off and the test signal cannot be read.

The STANDBY command (0022h) disables all channels and powers down the reference and other circuits while keeping register contents; stop CLKIN to save most power. WAKEUP (0033h) returns to conversion; modulators restart 8 tMOD after CLKIN resumes.

For tamper detection at low power. From standby only, a SYNC/RESET low pulse shorter than tw(RSL) starts it (with CD_EN set). The device runs from its internal oscillator at a nominal 2.7 kSPS, compares the absolute value of each result with the CD_TH threshold over CD_LEN conversions (128 to 3584), and when CD_NUM crossings occur on any enabled channel (or on all, with CD_ALLCH) pulls DRDY low and returns to standby. Results are not readable. Do not toggle CLKIN in this mode and keep REFIN free of capacitance, since a charging REFIN makes the results invalid.

The device is always the SPI slave in mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1): output changes on SCLK rising edges and input is latched on falling edges, full duplex. CS low selects the device; CS high resets the interface and puts DOUT in high impedance. CS is held low for the whole frame.

Active-low data-ready output; in current-detect mode it flags a detection. DRDY_SEL[1:0] picks the channel it follows: the most lagging phase setting (default), any channel, or the most leading. DRDY_HiZ makes it open-drain (pull up with 100 kΩ). DRDY_FMT selects a level that stays low until data are read, or a short pulse; in pulse mode an unread result suppresses the next pulse. A conversion finishing during a read blocks the pulse, so reads avoid that moment. The first DRDY after enabling or a sync can come within one sample period for negative phase settings, unless the setting is at or below the OSR boundary (-19 at OSR 128, -83 at 256, -211 at 512, -467 at 1024), when it moves to the next period.

Traffic is in frames of words of 16, 24 (default) or 32 bits, set by WLENGTH[1:0]. A normal frame is ten words: on DIN the command, its CRC (or zeros), then eight zero words; on DOUT the response to the previous frame's command, eight channel results and a CRC. Commands, responses, CRC and registers are 16 bits, MSB-aligned and zero-padded. RREG of several registers and WREG of several registers lengthen the frame. With TIMEOUT set, a frame must complete within 2^15 CLKIN cycles or the SPI resets, which recovers framing when CS is tied low.

Results are 24-bit two's complement; a 16-bit word truncates the eight LSBs, a 32-bit word zero-pads or sign-extends. 1 LSB = 2.4 / Gain / 2^24. Inputs at or above +FSR - 1 LSB read 7FFFFFh; at or below -FSR read 800000h. DRDY[7:0] in STATUS, sent as the NULL response, shows which channels have new data.

Each channel buffers two results, and its DRDY flag stays set until both are read. After a pause in reading, either pulse SYNC/RESET to resynchronize and clear the buffers, or read two frames back to back. In level mode a very narrow DRDY pulse follows the first read and can be missed by a host, so the second read is made at once.

NULL returns STATUS; an invalid command answers like NULL. RESET answers FF28h when performed and 0011h if the frame was cut short. STANDBY and WAKEUP have no effect when already in that state. LOCK leaves only NULL, RREG and UNLOCK active while data keep flowing. RREG of one register returns its contents in the next frame's response word; RREG of several returns an acknowledgment and then the registers in address order, without channel data. WREG writes each word as it arrives, so a CRC error cannot stop a bad write; read-only and out-of-range addresses are skipped though still counted in nnn nnnn, and the response gives the number actually written less one.
With all ADCs disabled, frames may carry just the command and response. With ADCs on, every output word is read each period. RESET always needs a full frame.

A SYNC/RESET low pulse longer than one CLKIN period and shorter than tw(RSL) compares its falling edge with the internal data-rate clock; if they differ, the filters restart in step with the pulse and F_RESYNC sets. Phase settings are kept, so shifted channels give results within one period, unsettled until three sinc3 conversions have passed. In global-chop mode conversions restart at once.
Unused analog inputs may float or go to AGND. Digital inputs are tied to DVDD or DGND, never floated, to avoid supply leakage. DRDY may be left open or pulled to DVDD with a weak resistor.

Each input needs an analog low-pass ahead of it. The digital filter rejects most out-of-band signals up to the region round fMOD, so a single RC stage per channel is enough in most designs; its values balance cutoff, source impedance and the charge the filter capacitor supplies to the sampling input.

CLKIN needs an LVCMOS clock from the host or a local oscillator. SYNC/RESET may be tied to DVDD and DRDY left open, but one of them goes to the host to keep it synchronized; if the host makes CLKIN it can instead count clocks, though a clock bit error then cannot be recovered. CS may be tied low when the device is alone on the bus, with both CRCs on.

All devices take the same CLKIN and have SYNC/RESET strobed together at least once; phase settings may differ, with the host tracking which channel is phase zero. They share SCLK, DIN and DOUT with separate CS lines (DOUT floats while CS is high), and one DRDY is enough because all convert together.

In the three-phase meter the host supplies an 8.192 MHz CLKIN, the device runs in HR mode at OSR 512 (8 kSPS), every channel at gain 1 on its own pins with zero phase setting, and the host SPI runs at 8.192 MHz with CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1, reading on each DRDY falling edge. Offset, gain and phase are calibrated once at room temperature; the DC block filter can stand in for offset correction.

An internal LDO makes the 1.8 V core supply from DVDD and brings it out on CAP. With DVDD above 2.7 V, CAP takes 220 nF to DGND. With DVDD at or below 2 V, CAP is tied to DVDD and the joined pins take 100 nF to DGND.

Supplies may come up in any order, provided analog and digital inputs stay inside their supply limits. AVDD and DVDD each take 1 µF, low-ESR MLCC, close to the pins; several vias in parallel to ground planes lower inductance. Join AGND and DGND close to the device.

Give a whole layer to ground with no traces; if planes must be split, join them once, at the ADC. Keep digital traces away from the analog inputs. Use C0G capacitors on the inputs and X7R-type ceramics for decoupling, not Y5V, close to the pins with short traces. A clean, glitch-free CLKIN matters; a series resistor at the clock driver tames overshoot. Two PCB layers are the minimum.
